contents.text:
I'm working out what to give the user: the page's listing is the coding agent's program, but they want a whole program to start their own agent. So I'll offer a template with their own catalogue, and be upfront that I don't know how to write a custom catalogue from the docs; the page only shows the coding agent's version, and the build-your-own guide covers the rest.

I'll note that the page's listing includes the using lines and keep them, since they belong to the program. I also need to flag that the "Usage" comment is in the code, so I'll include it exactly as written. I'm not going to invent a catalogue API. I'll offer the next steps: building an identity, building a pack, or walking through the page.

arguments.question: What next for your own agent?

choices.label: Build an identity
choices.why: Decide who your agent is, in markdown.

choices.label: Build a pack
choices.why: Give your agent a tool of its own.

choices.label: Walk me through this page
choices.why: Go through the getting-started sections in order.
